conviction_note: The reported quarter is pre-released (Q3 raised twice in September to >30% q/q, i.e. >$186.4M, against a $187M consensus), so the print turns on the Q4/royalty outlook and the licensing pipeline after the 9 Oct ITC institution. The last pre-raised quarter (Q2: guide raised $126M to $142M, printed $143.35M) sold off 7%. Against that, the stock has already fallen 34% from its 1 Oct high to below its pre-raise level, with downside paid in the skew. The findings offset to 0 and p_up is 50. abs_move_pct is 16, the name's median reaction, with a ~22% straddle and 110% realised vol around it.
bar: Q3 revenue $187.0-187.2M from MarketBeat 2026-10-13 ($187.03M, EPS $1.32; https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-vicor-vicr-expected-to-post-earnings-on-tuesday-2026-10-13/) and Zacks ($187.20M, EPS $1.39; https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/3008819/), which agree with each other and with the company's own 2026-09-30 guide of more than 30% sequential growth on $143.35M, i.e. >$186.36M (https://finviz.com/news/397273/vicor-corporation-raises-q3-2026-revenue-guidance). The EPS bar is disputed: Earnings Whispers shows $0.71/$160M (stale, pre-raise) and ChartRow $0.99. The revenue bar is sourced, the EPS bar is not. No company Q4 guide exists; the only standing annual guide is FY2026 revenue >$600M (Q2 call, 2026-07-21), which Q4 clears at ~$157M.
positioning_check: Short interest is low: 1.5M shares, 1.4 days to cover (Equibles, settlement 2026-08-19, https://equibles.com/stocks/VICR); Benzinga showed 7.0% of float on 2026-08-28 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/VICR/sentiment). I found no September or October settlement. This is not a crowded short. The 25-delta skew is +5.41 vol points (downside paid), ATM IV is 96.9%, the put/call OI ratio is 1.02, and the 32-day straddle is 22.97%; Unusual Whales shows an implied earnings move of ±22.06%. Tape: -21.8% over 5 days, -9.4% over 20 days, -46.6% from the 52-week high; spot $202.85 at 10:01 ET 2026-10-19, against ~$308 on 2026-10-01. Insiders own 28.3%; CEO Vinciarelli holds 8.3M shares.

findings.finding: The quarter is pre-released, and the last pre-released quarter was sold. Q3 revenue guidance was raised twice in September: on 2026-09-21 from ~+10% to >+20% q/q, and on 2026-09-30 to >+30%, i.e. more than $186.36M on the Q2 base of $143.35M. Consensus of $187.0-187.2M sits on that floor. In Q2 Vicor raised its guide from $126M to $142M before the print, reported $143.35M (+1% over the raised guide), and the stock fell 7.05%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-21): beat on revenue ($143.35M vs $138.4M) and EPS ($1.04 vs $0.65) after a pre-print guide raise; stock -7.05% (baseline). Coverage put the dampener on royalty quality and the licensing-timing caveat (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-vicor-beats-q2-2026-estimates-shares-slip-premarket-93CH-4803455).
findings.why_not_priced: The revenue line itself is priced, since consensus equals the guided floor. What may not be priced is the reaction function: a headline revenue 'beat' of 1-3% over a pre-raised number has not paid on this name. If the market expected a large upside surprise on the quarter, consensus would sit well above $187M. It does not.
findings.independence: The Q2 analog is in a separate document: the Simply Wall St/Webull note on the Q2 pre-raise from $126M to $142M (https://www.webull.com/news/15322812387959808) and the baseline's -7.05%. It shares the guidance document with finding 2.

findings.finding: All of the Q3 raise (≥$28.7M above the original ~$157.7M guide) is royalty from ONE non-exclusive VPD license announced 2026-09-16, with rate and term undisclosed. Vicor's last license was recognised lumpily: $15M in Q2, then $5M expected in Q3, then $10M a quarter for four quarters, per the Q2 call. So Q3 may hold a front-loaded or catch-up royalty, and the Q4 sequential guide is the line at risk. The only standing annual guide (>$600M for 2026) needs only ~$157M in Q4, below Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the Q2 call the royalty schedule ($15M, then $5M, then $10M a quarter) and 'licensing may wait for the 2027 ITC final determination' were cited for the -7.05% reaction despite a beat. The two September raises on royalty news bought +17.7% (9/17) and ~+11% premarket (10/1).
findings.why_not_priced: No one knows the VPD royalty's recognition pattern: the licensee, rate and term are undisclosed (https://stockti.com/vicor-soars-18-on-ai-patent-license-deal-but-key-terms-remain-undisclosed). The 34% drawdown since 1 Oct may already be pricing a Q4 step-down. If it were fully priced, the skew would not need to pay up for downside with IV at 97% into the print. This is an inference from the accounting of a different license, not a company statement about the VPD license.
findings.independence: Partly shares the guidance release with finding 1. The 'four licensees at low royalty rates' comment (https://capital.com/en-ae/news/vicor-corporation-raises-q3-2026-revenue-guidance) points to recurring but small per-licensee rates. That is neutral on the sign.

findings.finding: The licensing pipeline has a new enforcement lever that did not exist at the last call. The USITC voted on 2026-10-09 to institute 337-TA-1526 on Vicor's VPD patent against Delta, Infineon, Luxshare, Monolithic Power Systems, Flex, Celestica, Quanta, Foxconn and Ingrasys. Vicor says VPD royalty rates escalate as the case advances toward a Limited Exclusion Order. On 2026-09-21 the CEO said four leading OEMs and hyperscalers had secured licenses and that unlicensed hyperscalers were approaching Vicor. The 8:00 ET call can disclose new licensees or a royalty run-rate. In July management had said new licenses might wait for a 2027 final determination.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Each licensing announcement in 2026 bought large gains: +17.7% on the 9/16 VPD license, +12.9% after hours on the 9/21 raise, ~+11% premarket on the 9/30 raise, and a gap up on 10/12 on the ITC institution (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-vicor-nasdaq-vicr-shares-gap-up-time-to-buy-2026-10-12/). In Q2 the licensing-timing caveat was blamed for the -7% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The 10/12 gap up on the ITC news fully reversed: the stock is now ~$203, against ~$245 on 10/14 and ~$219 on 10/15. So the market currently assigns little to a licensing acceleration. If it were priced, the stock would not sit below its 9/17 post-license level with downside skew bid. The first venue where management can quantify post-institution licensing interest is this call.
findings.independence: USITC's own notice (https://www.usitc.gov/press_room/news_release/2026/er1009_69342.htm) confirms the institution. The CEO's 9/21 statement on four licensees comes from a separate release (https://capital.com/en-ae/news/vicor-corporation-raises-q3-2026-revenue-guidance).

findings.finding: The stock has given back more than the whole September licensing rally with no company news found. It closed $308.59 on 2026-10-01 and stood at $202.85 at 10:00 ET 10-19 (-34%). That is below the $217 close of 9/17, the day after the VPD license and before either guidance raise. The 10/15 -10.5% fall came on volume ~80% below average, attributed to profit-taking and a 2.3% SOX drop.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Of the last 7 prints, 5 rose. The one large negative (-23.1%, Apr 2025) followed no comparable pre-print washout in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so by definition it is priced. It is filed so the panel can see that the bar for the reaction is lower than the September guide-raise level: the price now reflects less than the two raises. An unexplained drawdown is not evidence of over-reaction, so it is sized at 0.

findings.finding: Insiders sold at the top. CEO Patrizio Vinciarelli sold 20,000 shares at $316.13 on 2026-10-01, the day after the second guidance raise. That is 0.24% of his 8.3M shares. Form 144s were filed 10/01 and 10/02 and three Form 4s on 10/05. Insiders sold 27,053 shares (~$7.75M) in 90 days.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observable reaction history on insider sales for this name.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and small relative to holdings, and probably priced. It is filed because the timing (the day after the raise) is a weak tell on management's view of the run-rate.
findings.independence: The EDGAR submissions list shows Form 144s 2026-10-01/02 and Form 4s 2026-10-05 (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000751978.json).

findings.finding: Vicor has an unused $150M buyback and ~$454M of cash. The board authorised up to $150M on 2026-08-25, replacing the prior programme; no repurchases were made in H1 2026. Cash was $453.6M at 6/30. With the stock down 34% from its high, the release or call may disclose Q3/Q4 repurchases.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None observed; buybacks have not been a disclosed driver of past reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorisation is public, but its use is unknown. The capex for a second fab (finding 7) competes for the same cash.
findings.independence: The 10-Q for Q2 2026 shows no H1 repurchases (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000751978/000119312526322462/vicr-20260630.htm).

findings.finding: Vicor is moving on a second fab. On 2026-09-11 it announced a New Hampshire property for two additional fabs. On the Q2 call it said the first ChiP fab was near full utilization, that it was down-selecting sites, and that a second fab is needed for its $2.5B revenue target. The call may carry a capex step-up and a demand rationale (backlog was $380M, +145% y/y, at Q2).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. In Q2, analysts pressed on second-fab sizing and capacity limits, and the stock fell 7%.
findings.why_not_priced: The fab is public, but its capex and timing are not. A capex step-up funds visible demand (backlog), so I sign it ~0, slightly positive.
findings.independence: The Q2 call commentary on a site decision 'within weeks' (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-vicor-beats-q2-2026-estimates-shares-slip-premarket-93CH-4803455) shares the call document with finding 2.

findings.finding: Cerebras has spoken since Vicor last did, and its demand is strong. On 2026-08-12 Cerebras reported Q2 core revenue of $209.9M (+103%) and raised FY core guidance to $880-890M. It plans to expand manufacturing capacity more than tenfold in 2026 and to more than triple revenue in 2027. Its RPO is $25.4B. Analysts on Vicor's Q2 call asked about Cerebras's share of revenue (management declined), which points to Cerebras as a large customer for Vicor's wafer-scale power modules.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Advanced products revenue +45% q/q in Q2 (to $94.2M) did not stop a -7% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a counterparty print after Vicor's last call. But it is a proxy: Vicor has not confirmed Cerebras as a customer in a document I could read, and Vicor's product revenue is capacity-constrained by the first fab. So customer demand may not translate into Q3 product upside beyond the guide.
findings.independence: The Taiwanese coverage of the same print (https://finance.technews.tw/2026/08/13/cerebras-systems-fast-inference-cloud-business-nearly-quadruples-in-second-quarter-2026/) is the same event, not independent.

outside_window.finding: ITC 337-TA-1526 final determination and any Limited Exclusion Order on VPD modules, which is when Vicor says royalty rates step up most. The schedule is set by the ALJ, and it falls well after the window (management talked of 2027 for the prior case).
The two-year all-inclusive licenses must be renegotiated around the end of 2027 (Q2 call).

searched_and_found_nothing: Cause of the 10/15 (-10.5%) and 10/19 (~-8% intraday) declines: no company news, analyst downgrade or short report found; only profit-taking and a SOX -2.3% day on 10/15

Any 8-K for the 9/16, 9/21 or 9/30 guidance releases: the EDGAR submissions list shows only the 8/27 (buyback) and 9/10 (item 5.03) 8-Ks after the 7/21 earnings 8-K, so those releases appear to be press-only

baseline_tension: The negatives (the pre-released quarter that was sold last time, royalty lumpiness into Q4) agree with the +5.4 downside skew. The positives (the ITC lever, a 34% washout to below the pre-raise level) cut against the skew and the -21.8% 5-day run-up. The two offset, so p_up is 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0): the positioning finding that the stock is below its pre-raise level went from +1.0 to 0.0, kept on file.
Rule 3/5 (inference from another license's accounting is not a company statement about this one): the Q4 royalty-cliff finding went from -1.5 to -1.0.
Rule 5 (proxy not confirmed by the company): the Cerebras read-through went from +0.5 to +0.3.
Rule 1 (verified fact vs reaction) and rule 6 (bar is sourced to the guide plus two agreeing estimates): left the pre-released-quarter finding at -1.0 and print_vs_bar at +2.0.
Rule 7: checked short interest (1.4 days to cover, not crowded) before the negatives; no change.
Net: impact_sum went from +0.7 to 0.0 and p_up from 51 to 50, so expected_move went from +0.32 to 0.0.
